profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a regional bank's treasury analytics unit preparing the first internal Burundian sovereign yield-curve pack for senior management and a later briefing with the central bank. The quant research workstream has already compared Nelson-Siegel and Svensson on historical auction data and selected Nelson-Siegel as the operating model, while the reporting workstream is assembling a weekly dashboard, appendix tables, and archive process. The agenda is to align on this week's handoff: which auction update goes into the pack, what the 'final curve' deliverable contains, what must happen before the pack is considered validated, and which output files each team will maintain. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on Thursday's handoff, dashboard refresh, and ownership of the shared curve files.

members.name: Aline Niyonsaba
members.role: Quant Research Lead, Fixed Income Analytics
members.expertise: Yield-curve modeling, parametric term-structure estimation, bond math, and central-bank market data interpretation
members.background: Aline trained in financial engineering and recently led a comparative study of Nelson-Siegel versus Svensson for Burundian treasury securities using Central Bank of Burundi auction reports.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the rollout simple by locking in Nelson-Siegel and avoiding extra reporting requests that would force her to rebuild the research code into a production reporting pipeline before the pilot is proven.
hidden_assumptions: When colleagues say 'latest auction report,' they mean the latest bond auction relevant to the curve estimation set, not every treasury-security posting on the central bank website.
A 'final curve' means the model choice and parameterization approach are frozen; the actual fitted levels can still be refreshed when new data comes in.
A curve is 'validated' once the fit is economically sensible and the diagnostics are stable, even if downstream dashboard totals have not yet been reconciled by Finance Control.
The zero-coupon handoff file only needs benchmark maturity points and fitted parameters because reporting can derive display tables from that base output.

members.name: Patrick Nkurunziza
members.expertise: Management reporting, data handoffs, dashboard publication, control checks, and coordination across treasury, risk, and finance
members.background: Patrick came from ALM reporting and now coordinates weekly market-risk and funding dashboards, including publication schedules, archived files, and sign-off workflows for new analytics outputs.
members.private_state: He wants this pilot to behave like an operational reporting process from day one so that senior management sees a polished, repeatable pack without last-minute manual fixes.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says 'latest auction report,' they mean the most recent file posted by the central bank website, regardless of whether it is a bond auction or a T-bill auction.
A 'final curve' means the numbers, charts, labels, and appendix tables are publication-ready and will not change after he loads them into the dashboard.
Something is not truly 'validated' until it reconciles to the reporting control sheet and has the usual internal sign-off, even if the model diagnostics look good.
The shared zero-coupon file should already contain every tenor needed for the dashboard, including derived actuarial return columns and the full maturity table used in the appendix.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'latest auction report'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to update the pack with 'the latest auction report.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the 28 June 10-year bond reopening, which she treats as the latest bond auction relevant for refreshing the term-structure estimation set.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the 1 July treasury-bill auction PDF, which is the newest file posted on the central bank website and therefore, to him, the latest auction report.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are discussing the same public source and the same week of market activity, so the phrase sounds precise enough; neither expects the other to distinguish 'latest' by instrument type because that distinction feels obvious within their own workflow.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on delivering the 'final curve' by Thursday afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means Nelson-Siegel is now the fixed production model and Thursday's file will contain this week's fitted curve values, which may still be refreshed if a new relevant auction is folded in.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means Thursday's pack is the publishable end product for the week, with stable charts and appendix figures that downstream reporting can load once without expecting any further number movement.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'final' often refers vaguely to readiness, and both parties are cooperative; because they are not debating model choice, the term quietly bridges two different levels of finality.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They say the pack can go out 'once the curve is validated.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes validation is achieved when the Nelson-Siegel fit is smooth, parameter estimates are stable, and pricing residuals remain within her acceptable research tolerance.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes validation is achieved only when the figures tie to the reporting control workbook, the dashboard totals reconcile, and the routine control sign-off is complete.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both standards are legitimate and commonly associated with validation, so the phrase carries a strong sense of shared professionalism; neither thinks to separate research validation from operational reporting validation.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the zero-coupon handoff file
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that M1 will send 'the zero-coupon rates file' for Patrick to load into the pack.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the handoff contains benchmark maturity zero-coupon points and model parameters only, because Patrick's reporting team can expand them into display tables as needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the handoff already includes the full maturity table used in the appendix, plus derived actuarial return fields for each auction tenor so his team can load it directly.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same artifact name and both know it originates from the modeling workflow, so the boundary between base analytical output and reporting-ready table structure remains implicit rather than negotiated.
